text:
Carla (PM): Heads-up — competitor just announced an "edge-lite" offering with aggressive per-token pricing and a 100–150ms 95th latency claim. Article: https://technews.example/edge-lite-launch. We need a quick decision: parity (match price/latency) vs lean differentiator (quality + routing). Thoughts?

Sanjay (Eng): We can do a narrow parity play if we accept lowered density (more infra cost) or push quantized variants. Short term: we could offer a 'low-latency' config that prioritizes small batch sizes + CPU offload, but perf vs cost tradeoff is real.

Mike (GTM): Sales getting a lot of churn signal from SMBs about price. If we don't respond quickly they'll push pilot deals to competitor. But enterprise deals value our SLAs and private options.

Elaine (Design): If we go parity on latency/price, we need messaging that emphasizes reliability and predictable SLAs, not just raw latency numbers. UI should surface cost vs latency toggles.

Ashley (Sales): +1 on quick price option for SMBs. Can we create a promotional 'edge-economy' tier for pilots for 3 months? That buys time while eng explores optimizations.

Priya (Solutions): A checklist for pilots: (1) SLOs (latency + availability), (2) integration guide for light SDK footpring, (3) clear fallback plan to higher-tier model if quality drops. We need sample prompts to validate quality regression.

Sanjay (Eng): Proposal: 1) 2-week feasibility spike to implement a low-latency config and measure 95th p95/p95. 2) Parallel spike on prefix-KV caching tweaks to reduce tokens for common prompts. 3) If metrics look good, ship a controlled promo for pilots.

Carla (PM): Agree. Let's define launch criteria before the spike finishes. Draft:
```
- Perf: 95th latency <= 160ms for our small-gen workload (seq<=128)
- Cost: unit cost delta <= 20% vs competitor pilot price
- Quality: paraphrase/QA evals <= 3% regression on our prompt set
- Ops: auto-fallback route available + telemetry enabled
- GTM: one-pager and pilot pricing doc ready
```

Mike (GTM): Those criteria look actionable. For pricing we should cap promo to 3 months and require credit card on file. Sales ops will help set limits.

Ashley (Sales): I'll draft pilot playbook and list 6 at-risk accounts to offer. Need engineering ETA to promise a pilot start.

Sanjay (Eng): Realistic ETA after spike: 3 weeks to pilot-ready. Spike owners: me (runtime), @Elaine for UX changes, @Priya for integration docs.

Elaine (Design): I'll mock up a compact 'latency/cost' toggle and a tooltip explaining tradeoffs by EOD Friday.

Priya (Solutions): I'll assemble prompt suite and run baseline evals against current model today. Share results by Tue.

Carla (PM): Decision: run Sanjay's spike now. If spike shows perf within criteria, we run a 3-month pilot promo and a lightweight UI toggle. If not, pivot to differentiator messaging (quality + routing) and a targeted enterprise upsell. Action items:
- Sanjay: start spike (owner) — due +2w
- Priya: prompt suite + evals — due +3d
- Elaine: UI mock — due Fri EOD
- Mike/Ashley: pilot playbook + target accounts — due +1w
- Carla: finalize launch criteria doc and pilot terms — due +3d

Sanjay (Eng): Starting spike now. Will post perf logs in this thread and create a short runbook with experiment configs.

deploy-bot: New experiment created: exp/edge-econ-spike-1774044321. Current status: queued.

Ashley (Sales): Thanks — will start outreach contingent on pilot readiness. :thumbsup:

Carla (PM): Great. We'll sync Friday 10am to review early spike telemetry and decide go/no-go for promo.

Mike (GTM): Keep the messaging draft simple: "Edge-economy pilot — low-latency option for lightweight workloads, backed by Redwood SLAs." We'll iterate after data.

Sanjay (Eng): First perf run queued; posting logs in ~2h.

Priya (Solutions): Eval baseline posted: small regressions on long-form summarization but within acceptance for chat/assist flows. Sharing details in the doc.

Carla (PM): Nice. If we hit perf but see quality regressions in long-form, we can gate the pilot to single-turn/assist use cases only. That keeps risk low.

Elaine (Design): Mock uploaded: /files/edge-econ-toggle-v1.png. Simple toggle + learn-more modal.

Carla (PM): Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene at Fri 10am. If anyone uncovers fatal regressions before then, please flag immediately in #incident-ops and here.
